subject: gnomeTinkerer
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: gnome tinkerer with a backpack of gadgets.
Style: whimsical low-poly mix.
reasoning:
Looking at the render, the hat band appears as a large dark brown cylinder sitting low over the forehead, nearly covering the eyes — I'm checking whether the brim proportions still read correctly underneath it.

The legs show pants with jagged torn flaps intersecting the boot shaft, creating a zigzag mismatch, though the small brass buckles floating at the sides look fine.

In the side view the legs sit noticeably forward of the torso, with hips and backpack offset in depth, feet positioned a bit ahead, and a large brass boiler tank protruding from the body that I need to check doesn't clip oddly.

The tank currently hangs below and beyond the backpack's sides, reading like a floating bedroll rather than a mounted component, so I'm narrowing its width and repositioning it higher so it tucks in and overlaps the bottom of the pack properly.

Now I'm noticing a dark navy block that looks like a hammer head poking out near the chest/pack area — the handle is buried inside the pack geometry while the head awkwardly sticks out on top. I should either relocate it to sit visibly lashed on the pack's side, or just remove the hammer piece entirely to avoid the clipping issue.

I'll settle the hammer at x -0.115 fitting within the pack width, keeping clear of the wrench pocket on the right. Checking the rotor blades floating above the head read fine as a flat line in side view, and reviewing the face: oversized gnome nose, eyes slightly askew, beard covering most of the mouth—acceptable overall.

Now looking at hip details: lantern hanging from a string, spyglass poking out behind the shoulder, both working fine. The boots and legs are jagged where the cylinder meets the leg sweep, so I want to adjust the boot shaft radius to be a bit wider than the pants cuff so the pants tuck cleanly into the boot at the ankle.

I'm tuning the radii so legs don't touch at center while still covering the pant-to-boot seam — bumping shaft and cuff sizes up slightly until the geometry overlaps cleanly without z-fighting.

I'm also adjusting the hat band dimensions to be thinner and lighter, checking its inner radius against the hat cone's base radius so they align without gaps at the seam.

For the face, I'll bump up the eye size slightly for more presence, enlarging the eye sphere radius, pupils, and pupil offset proportionally, plus a small highlight to give them a bit of sparkle.

Now I'm repositioning the hammer, replacing the rod and head placement so it attaches more naturally to the chest bone, shifting its z-depth and adjusting the handle and head geometry to match the new mount point.

I'm also reworking the tank assembly—adjusting cylinder length, torus positions, cap placement, and valve height so it fits correctly within the pack's z-span without sticking out the bottom, tweaking depth coordinates to keep it visually tucked under the pack.
